title: Windowed output reweighting + scheduled-billing credit probe for hosted per-token pricing
creator: Avery Chen
description: Investigate a paired approach to reduce marginal cost pressure on high-output streaming sessions by (A) applying a short-duration output-token reweight multiplier for long-running streams, and (B) introducing a scheduled-billing credit that smooths minimums across session windows. This ticket defines the experiment hypothesis, telemetry, rollout plan, and enterprise/SQ checklist required before canarying to production.
hypothesis: For hosted API customers, applying a small output-token discount (reweight <1.0) for streaming sessions that exceed a configurable session-length threshold, coupled with a scheduled-billing credit that offsets minimums when customers cluster requests into long windows, will: 1) reduce average per-request unit cost for heavy-output conversational apps, 2) keep perceived price fairness for short sessions, and 3) increase committed enterprise revenue by reducing churn from perceived over-billing on bursty streaming usage.
experiment_design: Cohorts: control = current per-token ing/egress metering; variant A = output reweight multiplier of 0.85 applied to egress tokens after 30s of continuous stream; variant B = variant A + scheduled-billing credit (windowed 1h buckets that allow negative carry-up to next bucket up to configured cap). Enrollment: opt-in for self-serve customers via flag and explicit opt-in for enterprise customers (SQ checkbox). Duration: 6 weeks per cohort. Traffic split: 80% control, 10% variant A, 10% variant B initially; canary ramp to 25/25/50 if telemetry stable. Metering: log both raw and billable tokens to support downstream reconciliation. Billing: adjust invoice preview and console usage views to show "raw tokens" vs "adjusted billable tokens".
success_metrics: Primary: delta in $/1000 requests (expected reduction 6–12% vs control), revenue retention rate among engaged enterprise accounts (target +2% retention over baseline), no regression in median 95th percentile stream latency. Secondary: reduction in token-bill complaints to support by >=20%, no increase in billing disputes. Safety thresholds: if any cohort shows >1% unintended underbilling (>10k USD discrepancy) or customer complaints spike by >50% vs baseline, pause rollout immediately.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dry-run: validate metering code and invoice previews in staging. 2) Security/Legal/SQ review with template answers for enterprise questionnaire changes. 3) Canaries on non-production committed customers (select customers who opt in). 4) 7-day observability window; check telemetry and dispute signal. 5) Gradual production ramp 10% -> 25% -> 50% as thresholds met. 6) Full opt-out path via console toggle and immediate reconciliation job to correct invoices if a bug is found.
risks_mitigation: Metering mismatches: build one-off reconciliation job and store raw token logs for 90 days. Perception fairness: update invoicing UI to show both raw and adjusted metrics and a short explainer. Enterprise SQ: prepare filled SQ responses, KMS impact assessment, and audit log changes. Latency/regressions: test in perf harness with long-session synthetic streams. Legal: review TOS changes with counsel before wider rollout.
